evidence: Project identity specified: name='aidm-pilot-task-queue'
Purpose: A reliable prioritized in-memory task queue engine supporting FIFO/priority scheduling, task leasing, TTL expiration, deterministic state snapshots, and JSON serialization/deserialization.
Desired outcome: A small, real, independently versioned TypeScript project implementing a reliable in-memory task queue library with comprehensive automated test coverage.
Target users/actors defined (2): End users, Developers and software systems requiring a prioritized in-memory task queue engine with leasing and snapshot determinism

In-scope items defined (4): Domain models: TaskItem, TaskPriority, QueueConfig, TaskLease, Queue operations: enqueue, dequeue, peek, lease, release, expireStale, Persistence representation: deterministic JSON state serialization, JSON deserialization, schema validation...

Explicit exclusions / out-of-scope recorded (14): external databases, Redis, distributed consensus, clustering, HTTP API, REST API, gRPC, UI, frontend, authentication, authorization systems, cloud infrastructure, deployment infrastructure, unnecessary framework dependencies

Primary workflows specified (4): Task Enqueue and Prioritized Dequeue, Task Leasing and Release Lifecycle, Stale Task TTL Expiration (expireStale), State Serialization and Deserialization Round-trip with Schema Validation
Functional capabilities defined (4 requirements with behavioral specifications)

Business rules specified (12): FIFO ordering preserved within identical priority levels; Leased tasks cannot be dequeued by another worker until lease expires or is released; expireStale evicts tasks exceeding TTL or resets expired leases; State snapshot JSON serialization must be deterministic and schema-validated; TaskPriority determines scheduling preference; QueueConfig specifies default lease durations, TTL limits, and queue capacities; TaskLease tracks active leases with leaseholder identity and expiration timestamp; JSON serialization must be strictly deterministic (reproducible ordering); Deserialization validates state against schema before restoring in-memory queue; FIFO ordering strictly enforced within the same TaskPriority level; Leased tasks are hidden from dequeue until released or expired; expireStale reclaims expired leases and evicts TTL-exceeded tasks
Non-functional requirements defined (6 items across performance, reliability, usability)
Platforms: Node.js library / in-memory TypeScript module
Required technologies: TypeScript, Node.js
Architecture requires Product Owner decision: Deployment & Hosting Environment Model
Data persistence specified: In-memory data structures with deterministic JSON snapshot serialization/deserialization
External integrations specified (1): Consumable as an independent TypeScript module / library
Security requirements specified (1): No external network exposure, isolated in-memory execution, input schema validation

Measurable criteria defined (4): Automated test suite passing with zero regressions; Primary workflows demonstrable end-to-end; 100% automated test pass rate across unit and integration/E2E test suites; TypeScript compiler check passes with zero errors under strict mode
Definition of completion specified (4 items)

Risks evaluated (1 risks documented)
